one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: (1) Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 (source 25). Consensus is EUR 10.65 EPS on EUR 11.68bn sales, inside the EUR 11-12bn guide (sources 15, 1). The print itself is expected; the swing factor is the first 2027 commentary. (2) TSMC Q3 results in mid-October and the first hyperscaler Q3 capex updates late in the month. (3) FOMC on Oct 27-28. The supervisor's correction holds and has gone further: Polymarket's October market (about $21.4m volume) now has no change at 73.5% and a hike at 25.5% (source 35; Tech Insider had 60% no change on 09-30, source 36). The 78% 'another 2026 hike' figure is therefore mostly about December, so I no longer treat late October as a hawkish risk. (4) No MATCH Act outcome is possible: the Senate is out until the week of 11-09 (source 34). Base rates from ASML's own history (source 39): in earnings months (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct, n=79) the 1-month log-return sd is 10.5%, against 8.9% in other months. Normalised by trailing vol, earnings months run about 1.05x the trailing-vol-implied sd, against 0.89x otherwise, and 11.5% of them move more than 1.645 sd (7.6% in other months). The median earnings-month return is +3.5%. October closes over 2007-2025 ranged from -19.3% (2024) to +21.4% (2011). Trailing realised vol is 42% (63-day) and 46% (1-year), so an earnings-month sd of about 0.44/sqrt(12) x 1.05 = 13.4% fits. Following the supervisor's point that my round-1 1-month ladder was too narrow, I widen it from 12.5% to 14% sd, keeping Student-t (5 df) tails. I centre at 1,820 (+0.6%), giving a small nod to the positive earnings-month median and the reduced October hike risk, but I take no real directional view. P(>=spot) is 0.522; P(>=2170, +20%) is 0.083, which matches the one +21% October in 19 years.

fair_value.method: Blend of four methods at EUR/USD 1.1243. 2027E EPS EUR 51.73 (USD 58.16) x 34x = USD 1,977 (w 0.40). 2028E EPS EUR 62, less a 4% expected MATCH Act haircut = EUR 59.5 (USD 66.9), x 29.5x NTM = USD 1,974 (w 0.35). Base-rate anchor: spot x 1.04 = USD 1,881 from a pooled ASML/LRCX/KLAC/AMAT post-run-up sample (w 0.15). Mean analyst target USD 2,116 (w 0.10). Blended: USD 1,975.

inputs_detail.derivation: MarketScreener 2028 consensus: sales EUR 65.0bn and EPS EUR 68.3 at a 37.5% net margin, i.e. net income about EUR 24.4bn. That EPS implies about 357m shares, which needs heavy buybacks from the Q2-26 count of 384.5m. On about 375m shares, EUR 65bn x 36% net margin (the 2027 consensus margin of 35.7%) gives about EUR 62.4. ChartMill shows about EUR 53 (supervisor; staler and thinner). SEMI's 2028 WFE +14.1% (source 11) and Citi's TSMC 2028 capex of $86bn (source 29) back about 19% revenue growth. I take EUR 62, up from EUR 60 in round 1, and keep below-consensus margin and buyback risk in the bear case rather than in the central EPS.

A full DUV-immersion sales and servicing ban costs about 10% of 2028 EPS after redeployment (China is about 20% of 2026 sales; source 32). I raise the odds of enactment affecting 2028 from 35% to 40%. ndaa.ai (source 34) confirms the December four-corners compromise path, which bypasses the stalled Senate floor vote, so 'stalled' understated the odds, as the supervisor noted. I stay below 50% because whether MATCH survives in the compromise text, and how the Dutch align, remain open. 0.40 x 10% = 4%.

Today about 31x CY2027 (MarketScreener 30.5x) and about 33x blended NTM; the forward P/E was about 28x at the $1,575 low on 09-14 (source 32). Trimmed from 30x to 29.5x for the verified Fed hiking cycle (source 21) and because 2028 growth (+15-20%) is slower than 2027's (+35%). This sits near the low end of the 10-year range (22-64, median 37).

bear.story: AI capex digestion following the 2026-09-14 AI-pacing call, a December NDAA compromise that keeps the MATCH Act's DUV sales and servicing ban, and/or a Fed that keeps hiking in December and into 2027. 2028 EUV orders slip, 2028 EPS comes in flat to EUR 50-53 (the low ChartMill-type consensus) and the multiple falls to about 21-23x. Analogues: AMAT -22% to -38% after the 2021 and 2024 run-ups, LRCX -10% median after >+80% run-ups, ASML -31% after the 2021 peak and the 2022 (-57%) and 2024-25 (-45%) drawdowns.

base.story: 2026 lands at EUR 43bn and 2027 at about EUR 54-55bn with EUV capacity sold out. 2028 revenue is near the EUR 65bn consensus, giving EPS of about EUR 60-62 after some MATCH risk. Hyperscaler capex keeps rising (S&P Global: about $1.3tn in 2027). The market pays about 29x NTM in Oct-2027 under a Fed on hold after one or two hikes. That is about +8%, a little above the pooled semicap post-run-up median (+1% to +7%).

bull.story: The AI build-out extends into 2028-29: TSMC capex heads to $86-90bn, the 2028 +30% EUV capacity step is confirmed, High-NA ramps and the June 2027 Capital Markets Day raises the 2030 range above EUR 60bn. MATCH is dropped from the compromise NDAA, there is no recession (Kalshi 21%) and the Fed pauses. 2028 EPS reaches the MarketScreener EUR 68 consensus (with buybacks) at about 33-35x. Analogues: ASML +56-65% after the 2012, 2019 and 2020 run-ups, LRCX +145% after the 2025 run-up.

thesis_break_reason: A close near USD 1,250 (-31%) is about 21.5x 2027E EPS of USD 58.16, the floor of the 10-year P/E range (21.95). It sits just below the March-2026 low (1,248) and 21% below the 2026-09-14 AI-pacing close of 1,575.15, which was a sentiment-only selloff. Getting there would most likely need a fundamental cause: 2027/28 EUV push-outs or cancellations, a guidance cut at the January 2027 results, a memory capex reversal, or a December NDAA that enacts the MATCH DUV sales-and-servicing ban without a Dutch carve-out. The supervisor uses 1,200. I keep 1,250 because at about 21x CY2027 the market would already be pricing EPS cuts; 1,200 (20.6x) is within one bad month of ordinary volatility from that level and does not change the diagnosis.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my main facts: 2027 EPS EUR 51.73 is in EUR, the Fed hike is real, and the NDAA is stalled in the Senate. It added four points, which I followed up with 8 lookups. (a) 2028 consensus is higher and more dispersed than I assumed. MarketScreener (source 33) has EUR 65.0bn sales, 37.5% net margin and EUR 68.3 EPS; the EPS implies about 357m shares. A share-count-neutral check gives about EUR 62, so I raise 2028 pre-haircut EPS from EUR 60 to EUR 62. (b) The NDAA compromise text can bypass the Senate floor (ndaa.ai, source 34), so I raise the odds of MATCH enactment affecting 2028 from 35% to 40% (haircut 3.5% to 4%). (c) October FOMC risk is smaller: Polymarket's $21m October market has a hold at 73.5% (source 35). (d) Thin markets (Polymarket AI-bubble and recession at about $9k, the Manifold markets) no longer feed any number; only Kalshi recession (21%, deep), Polymarket Fed (deep) and Taiwan ($462k) remain as context. On the supervisor's question of how much weight four own-stock episodes can bear: not much. I widened the base-rate sample to LRCX and KLAC (sources 37-38). Pooled ASML/LRCX/KLAC forward-12m medians are +6.9% after trailing >+60% (n=111 overlapping, 21 independent episodes) and +0.7% after >+80% (n=42, 11 episodes), against an unconditional +21-26%. So my round-1 peer anchor (AMAT only, -22%) was too bearish. The peer evidence still says the post-run-up drift is near zero, not the usual +25%. The anchor moves from +2.5% to +4% (1,881). Valuation: P/E on 2027 = 1,977 (34x); P/E on 2028 = 1,974 (EUR 59.5 x 1.1243 x 29.5x; the multiple trimmed from 30x for the verified hiking cycle); anchor 1,881; analyst mean 2,116. Weights 0.40/0.35/0.15/0.10 give 1,975 (round 1: 1,965). Distribution: median raised from about 1,880 to about 1,900 (+5%), below fair value because of the near-zero post-run-up drift and late-cycle de-rating risk. 42% log-vol (trailing 63-day realised 42%, 1-year 46%) with Student-t (5 df) tails and a slightly heavier left tail for the December MATCH event, giving P(>=spot) 0.558 (was 0.545). Scenarios 1,150 / 1,950 / 2,750 at 25/50/25 (mean 1,950). 1-month: widened to 14% sd after checking ASML's earnings-month history (source 39); centre +0.6%. Where I differ from the supervisor: I keep a 1,250 thesis break (vs 1,200), and my fair value (1,975) is above its 1,880, because I use consensus-anchored CY2027 at 34x alongside the NTM leg. No option prices, implied volatility or files under priors/ were used.
